theory.intro: A quadrilateral has four sides. Read its equal-side ticks, parallel arrows and right-angle marks. A shape can have more than one name, so give the most specific name or all the names the question asks for.
facts: **Square**: four equal sides and four right angles.
**Rectangle**: four right angles and equal opposite sides. It need not have all four sides equal.
**Rhombus**: four equal sides and parallel opposite sides. It need not have right angles.
**Parallelogram**: both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal.
**Trapezium**: at least one pair of opposite sides is parallel. With this definition, a parallelogram is also a trapezium.
**Kite**: two pairs of adjacent sides are equal. Adjacent sides meet at a corner. With this definition, a rhombus is also a kite.
Matching tick marks show equal sides. Matching arrows show parallel sides. A small square marks a right angle. A missing mark does not show that an angle is not right or that two sides are unequal.
A square is also a rectangle and a rhombus. Rectangles and rhombuses are also parallelograms.
To name a shape by its corner letters, follow the corners around its boundary, clockwise or anticlockwise.
steps: Read the given right-angle marks, side lengths, equal-side ticks and parallel arrows.
Match the stated properties to the shape definitions.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the information, or all the names if the question asks for them.

workedExamples.solution_text:
All four corners have right-angle marks. Opposite sides have matching ticks.
Rectangle.
All four sides equal is not given, so a square is not guaranteed. Turning the diagram does not change the marks.

workedExamples.question_text:
Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square?
Give a reason for each answer.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Yes. A square has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so it meets the rectangle definition.
No. A rectangle can have two longer sides and two shorter sides. A square needs all four sides equal.

Following the boundary clockwise from $P$ gives $P$, $S$, $Q$, then $R$.
$PSQR$.

foundation.question_text:
A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the given information.
foundation.solution_text:
Four equal sides and four right angles give a square.
Square.

foundation.question_text:
A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the given information.
foundation.solution_text:
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel opposite sides.
Trapezium.
Exactly one parallel pair means it cannot be a parallelogram.

development.solution_text:
Turning the shape does not change the markings: four equal sides and four right angles.
Square.

Opposite sides are equal: $5$ cm and $3$ cm. All four corners are marked as right angles.
Rectangle.
The side lengths are not all equal, so it is not a square.

One pair of opposite sides is marked parallel.
Trapezium.
Only two right angles are given, so a rectangle is not guaranteed.

development.question_text: Which property does every rectangle have that a parallelogram need not have?
development.solution_text:
Every rectangle has four right angles.
A parallelogram need not have right angles.

development.question_text: Which property does every rhombus have that a rectangle need not have?
development.solution_text:
Every rhombus has four equal sides.
A rectangle can have two longer sides and two shorter sides.

development.question_text: State the two properties of the sides of a parallelogram that are always true.
development.solution_text:
Opposite sides are parallel.
Opposite sides are equal in length.

Vertices must be read in order around the shape, either clockwise or anticlockwise.
Reading around Tommy’s sketch gives $ABDC$, not $ABCD$.
Swapping the labels $C$ and $D$ makes it rectangle $ABCD$.

development.question_text:
A quadrilateral has two pairs of equal sides, the equal sides are next to each other, and no sides are parallel.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the given information.
development.solution_text:
The two equal pairs are adjacent: each pair meets at a corner.
Kite.
The stated lack of parallel sides rules out a rhombus or square.

development.question_text:
A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides and exactly one pair of equal angles.
Give its most specific name, and explain why it cannot be a parallelogram.
development.solution_text:
Trapezium.
A parallelogram must have two pairs of parallel opposite sides. This shape has only one pair.

mastery.question_text:
A quadrilateral has four right angles.
Its opposite sides are equal, but its adjacent sides are not.
Name it, and state the one change to its sides that would make it a square.
mastery.solution_text:
Rectangle: it has four right angles and two pairs of equal opposite sides.
Make all four sides equal while keeping the four right angles. It would then be a square.

mastery.question_text:
Ali says that any quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides must be a parallelogram.
Name a special quadrilateral that shows Ali is wrong, and describe how its equal sides are arranged.
mastery.solution_text:
A kite that is not a rhombus shows Ali is wrong.
It can have two equal shorter sides meeting at one corner and two equal longer sides meeting at another corner.
The equal pairs are adjacent, not opposite, so it is not a parallelogram.

mastery.question_text:
In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB$ is parallel to $DC$, $AB = 6$ cm, $DC = 10$ cm and the corner at $D$ is a right angle.
Name the most specific special quadrilateral that $ABCD$ must be, and give the reason.
mastery.solution_text:
A parallelogram has equal opposite sides, but the given opposite sides are $6$ cm and $10$ cm.
It is not a parallelogram. The given parallel pair makes it a trapezium.
The right angle does not make it a rectangle, because a rectangle would also have equal opposite sides.
Trapezium.
